results.title: Slow Internet Speeds Troubleshooting
results.snippet: 1. **Weak modem signal** — downstream signal below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV indicates line issues. 2. **WiFi interference or distance** — 2.4 GHz band congestion; customer too far from router. 3. **Peak-hour congestion** — shared neighbourhood node oversubscribed in the evenings (6–10 PM).

results.title: Modem Reboot Procedure
results.snippet: Reboot the modem when the customer reports: - No internet connection despite modem appearing powered on - Very slow speeds that did not improve after router restart

results.title: Device Compatibility — Approved Modems and Routers
results.snippet: Customers must use a modem on the ISP-approved list to receive full technical support. Unapproved modems may work but are not guaranteed to provision correctly or receive remote management commands (including `reboot_modem_remotely`).

results.title: DNS Issues Troubleshooting
results.snippet: - Websites fail to load but the customer can ping IP addresses directly (e.g., `ping 8.8.8.8` succeeds). - Browser shows "DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN" or "Server Not Found" errors. - Some websites work but others do not, seemingly at random.

results.title: WiFi vs. Ethernet — Troubleshooting Connectivity Differences
results.snippet: | Factor | Ethernet (wired) | WiFi (wireless) | |---|---|---| | Speed | Full subscribed tier | Up to 80% of tier (varies by band) |

<analysis>
I've gathered the following diagnostic evidence:

**Customer Profile** [tool:lookup_customer]:
- Jane Smith, active account since 2021, Gigabit 500 service tier in northeast (ZIP 10001)
- Equipment: NETGEAR CM500 modem, TP-Link Archer AX21 router

**Modem Status** [tool:check_modem_status]:
- Modem is online but showing critical issues:
  - Downstream signal: -12 dBmV (outside acceptable range; should be between -7 and +7 dBmV)
  - Upstream signal: 44 dBmV (acceptable)
  - **7 restarts in the last 24 hours** — indicates line instability
  - Uptime only 0.5 hours — modem just restarted
  - Signal quality rated as "weak"
  - Note flags: "Signal level outside acceptable range; frequent restarts indicate line issue"

**Connectivity Test** [tool:ping_customer_modem]:
- High latency: 287 ms (very high for local modem)
- Packet loss: 12.5% (significant)
- Status: degraded
- Note: "High latency and packet loss detected — possible signal or line issue"

**ISP Outage Check** [tool:check_isp_outage]:
- No active outages in the customer's area (ZIP 10001)

**KB Consultation** [kb:slow_speeds]:
- Weak modem signal (downstream below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV) indicates line issues
- The customer's -12 dBmV downstream signal is well outside the acceptable range

**Diagnosis**: This is a **line-level signal issue**, not congestion or WiFi interference. The modem's weak downstream signal and frequent restarts point to a problem with the ISP's line to the customer's home — likely a signal degradation issue that requires ISP line technician investigation. A simple modem reboot won't resolve this; the underlying line issue must be addressed.
</analysis>

<reply>
I've run some diagnostics on your modem and I found the issue — your modem is showing a weak signal coming in from our line, which is causing it to restart frequently and drop packets. This isn't something a simple reboot will fix; it looks like there's a line issue on our end that needs a technician to investigate. I'd like to schedule a tech visit to check the line and get this resolved for you. Does that work?
</reply>
